notes.summary: This chapter covers BODMAS, percentages, fractions and mixed numbers, decimals, squares, cubes and roots, powers of the same base, and approximation. IBPS and SBI Prelims usually set 5 to 10 'What will come in place of ?' questions in the quant section, so speed with number facts and smart rounding decides your score.
keyPoints: BODMAS order: Brackets (innermost first: ( ), then { }, then [ ]), Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. Division and multiplication are done left to right: 48 ÷ 4 × 2 = 12 × 2 = 24, not 48 ÷ 8 = 6.
Learn squares up to 30 and cubes up to 20: 23² = 529, 27² = 729, 13³ = 2197, 14³ = 2744, 15³ = 3375, 17³ = 4913.
Fast squaring: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², so 52² = 2500 + 200 + 4 = 2704. For a number ending in 5, multiply the tens digit by the next number and append 25: 85² = 8 × 9 = 72, so 7225.
Powers of the same base: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn). Convert to one base first: 8³ × 4² = 2^9 × 2^4 = 2^13.
Missing-number questions: move every known term to the other side with the inverse operation. ? ÷ 16 × 9 = 360 gives ? = 360 × 16 ÷ 9 = 640.
Mixed fractions: add the whole parts and the fraction parts separately. 3 1/4 + 2 2/3 − 1 5/6 = 4 + (3/12 + 8/12 − 10/12) = 4 1/12.

Approximation: round each number to the nearest easy value (24.98% to 25%, 1599.9 to 1600, √624.87 to 25), solve, then pick the nearest option. If options are within about 5% of each other, round more carefully.
Unit-digit check eliminates options fast: 37 × 63 must end in 1, and 37² + 63² must end in 9 + 9 = 8.
traps: Doing a multiplication before an earlier division (or addition before subtraction) instead of working left to right.
Opening brackets in the wrong order, or forgetting to change signs when removing a bracket that has a minus sign in front of it.
Mixing up square roots and cube roots: √729 = 27 but ∛729 = 9.
Rounding every number upward in approximation, which piles up error and leads to the wrong close option.
notes.examTip: Do simplification first in Prelims, aim for 30 to 40 seconds a question, and use fraction equivalents, unit digits and option elimination instead of full long calculation.

questions.text:
What will come in place of the question mark (?)
∛2744 + ∛1331 = ?

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
4.8 × 2.5 + 3.6 ÷ 0.4 = ?
questions.explanation:
By BODMAS, do the multiplication and division before the addition.
4.8 × 2.5 = 12.
3.6 ÷ 0.4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
12 + 9 = 21. (Adding first and then dividing gives the wrong value 39.)

1.25 + 0.075 + 12.5 − 3.025 = ?

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
? ÷ 16 × 9 = 25% of 1440

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
48 ÷ [12 − {18 ÷ (3 × 2)} + 1] = ?
questions.explanation:
Innermost bracket first: 3 × 2 = 6.
Curly bracket: 18 ÷ 6 = 3.
Square bracket, left to right: 12 − 3 + 1 = 10.
48 ÷ 10 = 4.8.

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
(√? + 13)² = 4 × 15²
questions.explanation:
Right side: 4 × 225 = 900.
So √? + 13 = √900 = 30 (taking the positive root).
√? = 30 − 13 = 17.
? = 17² = 289. (17 is only √?, not the answer.)
